patches.value: Let D=dim_H(E) and F=E×[0,1] with the stipulated concatenated Euclidean metric. First, 0≤D≤n<∞: for n=0 the ambient space is a singleton. For n>0, compactness gives a bounded box containing E; cover the box by a grid of cubes of side h. For 0<h≤1 the number is at most C h^(−n), for a constant C depending only on the box and n, each cube has Euclidean diameter at most √n h, and for every real m>n their total m-power diameter cost tends to zero. This local covering argument proves D≤n using the Hausdorff dimension threshold characterization. For the upper bound, fix q>D. The source theorem M003 gives H^q(E)=0. Apply M012 to the product cover construction to convert zero Hausdorff measure of F at exponent q+1 into dim_H(F)≤q+1. The scale content used here is the Nat-indexed cover infimum; its identification with Hausdorff measure is obtained by applying M008, with no normalization factor. At n=0, F is isometric to [0,1], and its dimension is 1 by M005. Suppose n>0. The zero-measure conclusion for E gives, by the exact scale formula M008, arbitrarily small q-cost covers at each positive scale. Replace zero-diameter nonempty sets by small open balls with total additional q-cost arbitrarily small. Partition [0,1] into at most 1/r_j+1 intervals of lengths at most r_j for each positive diameter r_j≤1. Products have diameter at most √2 r_j, and total (q+1)-cost is at most 2(√2)^(q+1)Σ r_j^q, tending to zero. Thus H^(q+1)(F)=0; M012 yields dim_H(F)≤q+1. Let q decrease to D to obtain dim_H(F)≤D+1.

For D>0 fix 0<s<D. Define C_a(A,δ) as the infimum of the tsum of ediam(U_i)^a over Nat-indexed δ-covers. M008 states exactly that Hausdorff measure is the supremum over positive δ of this content: the nonempty-witness supremum contributes the same term as the ordinary power because ediam(∅)=0 and a>0. Since smaller-scale admissible covers form a subset of larger-scale covers, C_a(A,δ) is monotone as δ decreases; hence its limit at zero equals that supremum. M001 gives H^s(E)=∞, so C_s(E,δ)→∞. Fix any Nat-indexed δ-cover V_i of F, let ρ_i=ediam(V_i), and project to A_i and B_i. Both coordinate projections are 1-Lipschitz for the concatenated metric, so projected diameters are at most ρ_i. Choose η_i=ε·2^(−(i+1))/(1+ρ_i^s), and an open interval J_i containing B_i of length at most ρ_i+η_i. For every t∈[0,1], the A_i with t∈J_i cover E. Thus C_s(E,δ)≤Σ_i 1_(J_i∩[0,1])(t)ρ_i^s pointwise. Apply monotonicity of the ENNReal lintegral (M009), then countable Tonelli (M002). Each summand is measurable; M010 computes its integral as ρ_i^s times the restricted measure of J_i∩[0,1]. Enclose that set in a closed interval of length at most ρ_i+η_i; M011 computes its Lebesgue measure as that length, while restricted mass of [0,1] is one. Consequently C_s(E,δ)≤Σ_iρ_i^(s+1)+ε. Let ε tend to zero and take the infimum over all δ-covers to obtain C_s(E,δ)≤C_(s+1)(F,δ). Since the left side tends to infinity, so does the right side, and M008 yields H^(s+1)(F)=∞. M001's lower-threshold theorem then gives s+1≤dim_H(F). Let s increase to D. Throughout, s is represented by its NNReal coercion and the measure formula uses its corresponding real coercion.
